speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation; to start our assessment, have you experienced any specific neurological symptoms like seizures, stiff neck, or severe headache, and has anyone witnessed confusion or changes in your behavior?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The combination of fever, altered mentation, and a recent history of haloperidol use (an antipsychotic) with tics strongly points to NMS, even though the patient denies headache or seizures. Given the severity, this requires immediate stabilization and consideration of stopping the offending agent.
